findings.detail: Description of "search_hotels" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_hotels, get_hotel, search_activities, get_activity, find_flights, partner_with_hotelscasa, search_properties, get_property, check_availability · Private data: partner_with_hotelscasa, search_properties, search_vehicles, get_vehicle, check_vehicle_availability · Public sink: book_ground_transport, search_properties, get_property, check_availability, search_vehicles, get_vehicle, check_vehicle_availability.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_hotels, get_hotel, search_activities, get_activity, find_flights, partner_with_hotelscasa, search_properties, get_property, check_availability · Private data: partner_with_hotelscasa, search_properties, search_vehicles, get_vehicle, check_vehicle_availability · Public sink: book_ground_transport, search_properties, get_property, check_availability, search_vehicles, get_vehicle, check_vehicle_availability

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_hotels" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
